key_insight: A first-principles-to-Monte Carlo workflow predicts when Cu-Ni-Al alloys form ordered L1_2 Ni3Al precipitates versus remain as solid solution, with composition controlling the phase pathway.
engineering_relevance: The results help design precipitation-strengthened Cu-based alloys that retain good conductivity while gaining strength from coherent gamma-prime Ni3Al precipitates.
method: Ab initio electronic-structure calculations to derive atom-atom effective pair interactions.
Concentration-wave theory to analyze ordering and phase stability.
Atomistic Monte Carlo simulations to map temperature-composition phase behavior.
evidence_signal: The modeled phase behavior shows three composition-dependent regimes that qualitatively agree with the experimentally determined phase diagram.
watch_item: The study is qualitative with respect to experimental agreement, so quantitative phase boundaries and kinetics may still require further validation.
paper_title: Formation of $\mathrm{L}1_2$-ordered $γ'$-$\mathrm{Ni}_3\mathrm{Al}$ precipitates in ternary Cu-Ni-Al alloys modelled using an ab initio concentration wave theory and atomistic simulations
